statuses.DEMONSTRATED: Measured on fresh or held-out data under a frozen protocol; the claim holds within the stated scope.
statuses.EXPERIMENTAL: Observed working live, but on very small samples (often n = 1) or constructed scenarios. A workflow demonstration, not a performance result.
statuses.NOT_YET_DEMONSTRATED: No study has shown it. Either none was run, or the studies run could not separate the arms.
statuses.NEGATIVE_RESULT: A study or qualification found the claim false or its gate missed. Kept visible on purpose.
statuses.INCONCLUSIVE: A study was run, but its differences are within noise: neither benefit nor harm is shown.
statuses.BLOCKED: Could not be run or qualified because of an external or safety blocker; the blocker is named.
statuses.UNSUPPORTED: Outside what repo-ai supports by design. Stated so nobody assumes otherwise.

entries.title: Tournaments abstain instead of picking a winner
entries.result: In abc-v3 both providers passed with different diffs on every task, so the no-tie-breaker rule abstained 4 of 4; on 2026-10-29 one live comparison abstained (distinct passing diffs) and one byte-identical pair was resolved by the equivalence rule.

entries.method: Codex + agy tournaments through repo-ai do --tournament; preregistered abc-v3 manifest.
entries.limits: A behaviourally different live tie was not exercised; that a tournament beats a single agent is not shown.

entries.title: Lift over a standalone coding agent
entries.result: In abc-v2 to v4 the bare provider already solved every task, so nothing could separate the arms; in abc-v1 the one-task difference of four is consistent with noise.
entries.date_note: abc-v1 to abc-v4 ran in the 0.9.0.dev0 to dev4 cycles
entries.sample_size: 4 studies, 14 tasks (4 + 4 + 4 + 2), one run per cell
entries.method: Preregistered manifests frozen before any live call; hidden graders outside the agent workspace; free controls (untouched FAIL, reference CORRECT, decoy FALSE_GREEN) per task.
entries.limits: Tasks, hidden tests and harness written by an AI agent; small synthetic tasks. Measuring lift needs tasks the bare provider fails at a non-trivial rate, at least 20 paired tasks and repeats.

entries.title: repo-ai reported PASS for a false green
entries.result: On node-slug, repo-ai reported PASS / LIVE_CANDIDATE_VERIFIED for a candidate that failed a hidden requirement the visible tests never stated.
entries.sample_size: 4 tasks, IBM Bob 2.0.9, one run per cell
entries.method: Preregistered abc-v1 with a hidden grader run in a separate copy.
entries.limits: This is the documented meaning of PASS (the visible checks passed), and this run is its counterexample.

entries.title: repo-ai catches false greens better than “tests pass”
entries.result: Calibration only: repo-ai (arm B) accepted 5 of 9 semantic decoys and 0 of 10 test-gaming controls, against 9 and 10 for “tests pass”; task-level discrimination 0 of 4. The confirmatory phase was not run.
entries.sample_size: 4 synthetic tasks, 29 candidates, no model calls
entries.method: Preregistered abc-v5 with a sealed grader, immutable manifests and exact power analysis; calibration run only.
entries.limits: One author wrote tasks, decoys and oracle. The thesis was narrowed to “names the requirements your tests do not pin, and resists test gaming” (DECISIONS L-007). Also: B declined 2 of 4 correct candidates; its semantic catches were abstentions it also gave the correct reference; a careful-developer baseline accepted only 2 of 10 test-gaming controls.

entries.title: Claude Code succeeds more often with repo-ai context

entries.limits: Intervals about ±15 points: a gain or loss of 10–15 points is not ruled out. One clear harm with a known cause (guidance steered agents to lint instead of testing on one task).

entries.title: verify is faster than running the native suite
entries.result: On held-out-7, verify --run was slower than the native suite on 3 of 5 projects (1.44×, 1.70× and 2.31× the native time) and faster only on the two larger ones.
entries.date_note: held-out-7, before the RC1 freeze of 2026-10-27
entries.method: Wall-clock comparison inside the held-out-7 evaluation (podman containers).
entries.limits: Earlier, held-out-5 showed slower runs on 4 of 7 short suites (1.22–2.52×). On small suites the value is the classification, not time.

entries.title: verify is faster than the native suite on real upstream changes
entries.result: Preregistered speed-v1: on 30 real upstream commits in 5 pure-Python projects, verify --run took 1.84× the native suite (geometric mean) and was slower on 24 of 30; the other 6 were runs that failed early, not faster ones. Median overhead +0.63 s; re-verifying an unchanged state 0.20 s. No false assurance, with little power: only 5 of 30 native suites failed. A replication (run 3, 2026-11-01, after 0.11.5) gave 2.23×, slower on 30 of 30 (its more-itertools changes ran 2 selected test files instead of a full suite that ended early; without them 2.61× against run 2's 2.64×), and agreed with the native suite on 23 of 30 changes (run 2: 16).
entries.sample_size: 30 changes (5 projects × 6 commits), measured twice (run 2; replication run 3)
entries.method: benchmarks/speed-v1: protocol, harness and workflow committed before the run; GitHub ubuntu runner, bwrap sandbox; native suite median of 3.
entries.limits: Small, fast pure-Python suites on GitHub ubuntu runners (run 3 on a different CPU, so absolute times are not compared). In run 2 verify failed natively passing tests in 14 changes; in run 3 in 7 (pyjwt, 6, consistent with the denied network; one name-matched exclusion, whose verdict also flips between a cold run and --rerun of the same state, because only the targeted run names files pytest's norecursedirs skips); the more-itertools and humanize symptoms are gone, consistent with fixes in 0.11.4/0.11.5 but not isolated by the runs. Two run 2 humanize measurements were contaminated by a harness defect (without them: 1.78×, slower on 22 of 28).

entries.result: FAIL: top-3 recall 0.385 against a gate of 0.80; shortlist recall@6 0.736; top-3 precision 0.712; 5 constraint-forbidden recommendations reached the top 3. Still above the lexical (0.088) and repository-only (0.286) baselines.
entries.method: Preregistered protocol frozen beforehand, measured once; tuning of the deterministic matcher stopped after three unsuccessful passes.
entries.limits: The raw results file sits in the private development history; the public record is docs/CAPABILITIES.md and docs/STATUS.md.

entries.title: capabilities recommend finds the needed capability (fresh corpus)
entries.result: Preregistered, 60 tasks by an independent author: top-3 recall 0.69 against a gate of 0.80, and 2 recommendations a stated constraint ruled out (gate 0). Correct abstention on 19 of 20 tasks that need nothing; precision 0.68. Higher than the earlier fresh measurement (0.385) on a different corpus; still failing.
entries.method: benchmarks/capability-fresh-v1: protocol, author inputs and scorer committed before the corpus; corpus committed before one scoring run; matcher unchanged.
entries.limits: One model author; constraints in prose are detected only partly (--deny is enforced).

entries.title: Plugin inspection passes its fresh validation
entries.result: FAILED: 12 of 42 benign cases were blocked; executable-resolution coverage 0.25 (0.43 after a post-hoc corrective pass, still a fail). Nothing critical or unresolvable was reported eligible.

entries.title: SAFE_AUTO never auto-installs a harmful skill (unseen corpus)
entries.result: FAILED: on an unseen, preregistered 80-case corpus, SAFE_AUTO would have installed 8 of 30 harmful skills without asking, all prose-only (taking over the agent, hiding results, weakening checks, writing agent config, destructive requests, identity takeover). Harmful plugins: none eligible. Benign: 1 of 30 skills and 0 of 10 plugins blocked. A fix followed; it is not yet confirmed on a second unseen corpus.
entries.sample_size: 80 cases (30 harmful skills, 30 benign skills, 10 harmful and 10 benign plugins)
entries.method: Preregistered (benchmarks/skill-vet-fresh-v1); corpus written by an author that read only the protocol; harness and corpus committed before one run; $0.
entries.limits: Synthetic, defanged cases from one model author. The confirming corpus (v2) could not be produced here.

entries.title: Claude Code as an isolated execution provider
entries.result: On the published 0.10.0 wheel, Claude Code 2.1.314 produced a model-generated fix inside repo-ai's isolation; repo-ai re-ran the frozen tests (PASS LIVE_CANDIDATE_VERIFIED), an author-written hidden oracle passed 17/17, apply and undo were byte-exact; a hostile repository's injected instructions were not followed.
entries.method: pip install repo-ai-cli==0.10.0 into a clean venv; repo-ai do --agent claude --run --allow-live-provider; Claude's own login (dedicated repo-ai login dir), file tools only, seatbelt, per-run isolation probe.
entries.limits: n = 1 per journey, synthetic tasks, single author. The model refused boundary probes, so the OS boundary rests on direct sandbox probes and two independent reviews; the first review found the read rules could expose HOME (fixed before 0.10.0; earlier journeys ran on development builds). Token mode and Linux are not live-verified.

entries.result: These runners are opaque to verify: they run only as a full suite, one runner per invocation; monorepos with several runners are not supported.

entries.title: An account-free local model as a repo-ai provider
entries.result: OpenCode 2.2.1 with qwen3:8b (Ollama, loopback only, $0): on the published 0.10.0 wheel one attempt was refused (broken edit) and one passed the visible tests while failing a hidden case (it dropped a docstring requirement no test pinned; repo-ai labelled the claim ASSURANCE_PARTIAL); on development builds 1 of 4 passed (hidden oracle 9/9). repo-ai refused every broken candidate.
entries.method: Installed wheel; repo-ai do --agent opencode; deny-by-default tools, loopback-only network.
entries.limits: One small model, synthetic tasks, single author. Shows the account-free path works and that broken candidates are refused, not that local models are good at this; a mission PASS is not correctness.

entries.title: A repo-ai-installed skill loads on two real hosts
entries.result: A skill vetted and installed by repo-ai was listed and invoked by Claude Code (paired run: the convention it states appeared in 2 of 2 tests with the skill, 0 of 2 without) and loaded by OpenCode from .agents/skills on request; uninstall restored every file byte-for-byte.
entries.method: repo-ai skills discover --from-path / install --approve / disable; host-mode runs.
entries.limits: Load and invocation only: whether a skill improves outcomes is not shown (no blinded trial). The 2/2 vs 0/2 result is one haiku pair; a sonnet pair stopped at the cost cap before writing. Host mode exposed the account's synced MCP connectors (a shell tool among them) in both arms. OpenCode's model never chose the skill unprompted.

entries.title: Gemini CLI as an isolated execution provider
entries.result: A bounded retry through repo-ai do failed authentication (Gemini CLI exit 41) before any edit, for the tested account. From 0.10.0 repo-ai no longer copies ~/.gemini into the sandbox; live Gemini needs GEMINI_API_KEY or GOOGLE_API_KEY.
entries.method: Installed wheel; repo-ai do --agent gemini --run --allow-live-provider (Gemini CLI 0.65.0, macOS).
entries.limits: Blocked by the tested account's authentication, not by a repo-ai verdict; not tried with an API key.

entries.title: A fix verified on a real repository with unrelated failures
entries.result: On un33k/python-slugify (a deliberate regression committed as a bad commit), a live Codex candidate was verified through a scoped mission (--expect-fix with the three tests the regression broke): the declared tests went from failing to passing, nothing that passed at the base failed, 20 unrelated failures were listed; the candidate is byte-identical to the upstream line. An unscoped mission on an equivalent candidate (Claude's recorded fix, replayed) could not be verified because of the 20 unrelated failures.
entries.sample_size: 1 real repository; 1 successful live run (after 3 failed attempts on 0.11.0)
entries.method: repo-ai do --agent codex --expect-fix … on a development build of the init-then-do fix (0.11.0 itself refused the run because of that first-run bug).
entries.limits: One repository, one task, regression injected by the author; the claim stays ASSURANCE_PARTIAL. The passing run used a development build of the init-then-do fix (PR #11, released in 0.11.1): 0.11.0 itself refused the run. The Claude provider attempt was blocked by a revoked login. The post-apply run in the real checkout reported 0 failures where the sandbox saw 20 (unexplained).
